title: Metrics & Monitoring Performance 📊
description: Track accuracy, precision, recall, and custom metrics during training.

slides.title: Why Metrics? 📈
slides.content:
# Loss ≠ Perceived Success

Loss is for the optimiser. **Metrics** tell humans how well the model does on tasks.

Examples:
- **Accuracy**: fraction of correct predictions.
- **Precision / Recall**: for imbalanced datasets.
- **AUC**: area under ROC curve.

You can track multiple metrics at once.

slides.title: Compiling with Metrics
slides.codeSnippet:
model.compile(
    optimizer='adam',
    loss='binary_crossentropy',
    metrics=['accuracy',
             tf.keras.metrics.Precision(),
             tf.keras.metrics.AUC()]
)

quizData.question: Which metric would you use for a highly imbalanced classification problem?
quizData.explanation: Accuracy can be misleading when classes are imbalanced; precision/recall give better insight.

slides.title: Custom Metrics 🛠️
slides.content:
# Subclass `tf.keras.metrics.Metric`

You can create your own metric by implementing `update_state` and `result`.

```python
class MyThresholdAccuracy(tf.keras.metrics.Metric):
    def __init__(self, threshold=0.5, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        self.threshold = threshold
        self.correct = self.add_weight(name='correct', initializer='zeros')
        self.total = self.add_weight(name='total', initializer='zeros')
```

slides.title: Reading the History
slides.content: `fit()` returns a History object with loss and metrics.
slides.codeSnippet:
history = model.fit(X, y, epochs=5, validation_split=0.2)
print(history.history.keys())  # dict_keys(['loss', 'accuracy', 'val_loss', 'val_accuracy'])

slides.title: TensorBoard Integration 📋
slides.content: Use `tf.keras.callbacks.TensorBoard(log_dir='./logs')` to visualise metrics in real time.
